items.text: No adult-use cannabis. Possessing 20 g or less of cannabis is a first-degree misdemeanour; more than 20 g is generally a third-degree felony. Concentrates and resin are excluded from the 20 g misdemeanour rule.

laws.rule: Recreational cannabis is illegal in Florida; only qualifying medical use under Florida Statutes 381.986 is allowed, for registered patients. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land such as national parks.
Florida's concealed-carry rule for non-residents covers only people who are residents of the United States, aged 21 or over. An Australian visitor living abroad is not covered by it.

Dry Tortugas National Park: the only fires allowed in the campground are charcoal briquettes in the campsite grills; gas camping stoves are allowed by the park, but the commercial ferries do not carry compressed gas canisters. Overnight anchoring for private boats is allowed only on sand and rubble within 1 nautical mile of the Fort Jefferson harbour light and must not block a channel.

Miami Beach says alcohol and smoking are always prohibited on its city beaches. During its March spring-break period the city also sets entry checks at Ocean Drive beach entrances for prohibited items, including coolers, glass containers and inflatables, and restricts amplified music without a city permit.

Miami Beach has treated March as a high-impact month (2026 measures ran Thursday to Sunday from 5 March, with peak weekends 12-15 and 19-22 March). Measures included Art Deco package liquor stores keeping to their 8 p.m. closing time, Ocean Drive open to vehicles only from 15th Street with one exit at 5th Street, beach entrances limited to 5th, 7th, 8th, 10th, 12th and 14th Streets with bag checks, rental golf carts, scooters and similar vehicles suspended, and DUI and licence-plate-reader details. Non-resident vehicles towed in the Art Deco area were charged double the regular rate. Dates and measures change each year, and the city has used curfews in some earlier years (for example 2024).

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Dry Tortugas National Park
layers.process: Dry Tortugas is about 70 miles (113 km) west of Key West with no road access; visitors arrive by ferry, seaplane, private boat or permitted charter. Everyone aged 16 and over needs an entrance pass: US$15 (about A$21) per person, valid 7 days, and the ferry ticket includes it. The park does not take cash. Camper seats on the Yankee Freedom ferry sell out months ahead (operator phone on the park page: 1-800-634-0939). Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Dry Tortugas National Park
layers.process: Camping is on Garden Key only. Regular six-person sites are first come, first served and cannot be reserved; anyone who arrives on the daily ferry is guaranteed a spot. The ferry carries at most 10 camping passengers a day, so camper ferry seats are the real limit. Groups of 10 to 20 must apply in advance for the large group site. Camping fee: US$15 per night per site (about A$21), US$30 for the large group site (about A$43), paid through the Recreation.gov Scan and Pay app (wifi is limited to the boathouse). A tent is required. Compressed gas canisters are not allowed on the ferry, so campers bring charcoal. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Everglades National Park
layers.process: A wilderness permit is required for all overnight camping outside the drive-in campgrounds, except when sleeping aboard a boat. Reserve on Recreation.gov up to three months ahead; the confirmation email is the permit, so carry a printed or saved copy. Fee: US$21 administrative fee (about A$30) plus US$2 per person per night (about A$2.85), for advance and walk-up permits. A credit card is needed. Campsites must be vacated by noon, and the page sets a night limit per site in the peak season, mid-November to late April. Chickee (raised platform) and ground sites allow no campfires; tents must be free-standing at chickees. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
activities: wilderness camping: Marjory Stoneman Douglas Wilderness

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Everglades National Park
layers.process: The standard entrance pass is US$20 to US$35 (about A$28 to A$49). The park states that non-US residents aged 16 and over pay an additional US$100 per person (about A$142) unless admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful pass. The park does not accept cash. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
